prerequisites: Elementary knowledge of Linear Algebra (Mathematics 1 for Computer Scientists)
Interest in algorithmic techniques and cryptography, in theory and practice (implemented with the help of the computer algebra system Sage).

learning_outcomes.text: Students should acquire broad knowledge of algorithmic techniques of asymmetric cryptanalysis, especially for coding-based cryptography.
Students know basic key-finding algorithms such as Brute-Force and Meet-in-the-Middle and can apply them to new cryptographic systems.
They master the basics of linear codes and their dual codes, especially the McEliece cryptosystem as a cryptographic application.
Students know Time-Memory techniques like Pollard Rho and Parallel Collision Search and can apply them to new problems.
Students have an overview of all current decoding algorithms in the field of Information Set Decoding, which are relevant for the security evaluation of modern coding-based cryptosystems.
Students are able to implement cryptanalysis techniques using the computer algebra system Sage.

syllabus_topics: Cryptanalysis for instantiating cryptographic systems to provide a predefined security level and optimize performance.
Algorithmic techniques for evaluating new cryptographic systems.
Algorithms for quantum computers to ensure security in a quantum computing era.
teaching_methods: Practical exercises on the computer with Sage (praktische Übungen am Rechner mit der Computer-Algebra Sage)
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded for a successfully passed written exam (Klausur). The exam duration is 120 minutes.
